You can pay up to £4,000 a year into a Lifetime ISA. That counts towards the £20,000 overall ISA allowance. The government adds a 25% bonus, up to £1,000 a year.

You can open a Lifetime ISA if you're aged 18 to 39. You can withdraw without charge in these cases:
- to buy a first home costing £450,000 or less, provided the account has been open for at least 12 months
- from age 60
- if you are terminally ill with less than 12 months to live

Other withdrawals incur a 25% government charge. More detail is in the ISA guide: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/isas/

The documents give these timescales for a complaint:

- If we can resolve it within three working days, we confirm that in a summary resolution letter.
- Otherwise, we acknowledge it in writing within five working days and tell you who is handling it.
- If the investigation can't be completed within eight weeks of receiving your complaint, we write to explain the delay. That letter says when we expect to respond and explains your right to go to the Financial Ombudsman Service without waiting.

If you're unhappy with our final response, or if eight weeks pass without one, you can refer the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service free of charge. If you're unhappy with our final response, you can refer the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service. It's free to do. You must do it within six months of the date of our final response.

- Telephone: 0800 023 4567, or 0300 123 9123
- Website: www.financial-ombudsman.org.uk
- Post: Financial Ombudsman Service, Exchange Tower, London, E14 9SR

The Financial Ombudsman Service's telephone numbers are 0800 023 4567 and 0300 123 9123.

Its website is www.financial-ombudsman.org.uk. You can refer a complaint to it free of charge if you're unhappy with our final response, or if eight weeks pass without one. You must do so within six months of the date of our final response.

It may not be too late. The Ombudsman can normally consider a complaint made within six years of the event. It can also consider one made within three years of when you became aware, or should reasonably have become aware, that you had cause to complain. Whichever of those is later applies.

If you're unsure whether your complaint is in time, contact us anyway. More details are on our complaints page: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/complaints/

For gains on investments sold in a general investment account, the capital gains tax annual exempt amount is £3,000.

Gains above that on shares and funds are taxed at 18% or 24%, depending on your total taxable income. You can set losses against gains in the same year. You can also carry them forward if you report them to HMRC. Income and gains within an ISA or pension are free of UK income tax and capital gains tax.

More detail is at https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/

Outside an ISA, dividends are tax-free within the dividend allowance of £500 a year. Above that allowance, they're taxed at:

- 10.75% for basic-rate taxpayers
- 35.75% for higher-rate taxpayers
- 39.35% for additional-rate taxpayers

Source: https://www.fernhillwealth.example/guides/tax/
